entries.text: My provisional reading is that the later argument qualifies the paved road rather than abandoning it: establish authority for protected access and actions, without making identity the price of exploring public information. This is my synthesis. The newer post is explicitly AI-written, so its publication is not evidence that the human author has committed to this exact position.
entries.scope: Public enquiries versus protected access and transactions

sources.quote: Prioritising agents that take this route over agents that don't seems reasonable.

entries.text: Separating enquiry from transaction may not settle the problem. Giving identified agents better access to a scarce public-information service could still pressure users to disclose their identity. The earlier prioritisation claim might apply only to transactions, might have changed, or might survive alongside this privacy concern. The archive alone does not decide between those readings.

entries.text: One reading of Gassing is that the change advocate and the newcomer judge unfamiliar language from different positions. Both perspectives are present in the same article. They need not be merged into one preference about jargon, and they do not establish separate psychological selves. A competing explanation is a single conditional principle: new language is worthwhile when it helps its users more than it excludes them.
entries.scope: Contextual stances towards new terminology; not a personality or clinical assessment

entries.text: Naming a persona can reproduce the very problem the article describes: a useful metaphor starts governing the person it was supposed to help explain. Keep the role-based and single-conditional-principle readings available. Ask about a concrete decision before asking the author to inhabit an invented identity.

entries.text: Architecture the easy way describes writing that passed through ChatGPT, Claude and human edits. Who is asking? explicitly labels its prose as AI-written. The shared domain therefore cannot be treated as a single speaker. A useful reader must keep authorship, permission to publish, agreement with an argument and commitment to act on it separate. Even a GitHub account cannot solve this: the agent building this system is using the owner’s authorised connection.
